title: E-Commerce Behavior: 5 Relational Tables (236K Rows)
subtitle: 10K customers, 120K transactions, 80K sessions, 25K reviews — all synthetic
description:
Five relational tables covering the full e-commerce lifecycle: 10,000 customer profiles, 1,000 products across 15 categories and 20 brands, 120,000 transactions, 80,000 browsing sessions, and 25,000 product reviews — 236,000 rows in total. All of it is synthetic, produced by the seeded generator (create_dataset.py) that ships alongside the CSVs, so it carries no personal data and anyone can regenerate or resize it.

The tables really do join. Every customer_id in transactions, sessions and reviews resolves to a row in customers, and every product_id in transactions and reviews resolves to a row in products — 100% referential integrity on all five foreign-key edges, checked in the companion notebook rather than asserted here. The price chain is consistent too: transactions.unit_price equals products.price x (1 - discount_applied/100) for all 120,000 transaction rows.

Built for churn prediction (is_churned on customers), lifetime-value regression, recommendation and market-basket work, RFM segmentation, conversion-rate optimization (converted/bounced on sessions), and multi-table feature engineering. The companion notebook shows what the join buys you: aggregating sessions and transactions onto the customer table lifts 5-fold churn ROC-AUC from 0.660 to 0.679 against a demographics-only baseline, and wins in all five folds.

Design notes: transactions carry completed / pending / refunded / cancelled statuses for realistic label imbalance; sessions record device, channel, duration, pages and cart additions for funnel analysis; customers span five value segments (VIP, Premium, Regular, Budget Shopper, Occasional Visitor) whose churn rates differ by design. Events span 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-30, with signup dates reaching back to 2020-01-01. Because it is generated rather than observed, it is meant for teaching, benchmarking and prototyping — not for drawing conclusions about real shoppers.

resources.description: 10,000 customer profiles with demographics, value segment, churn label and assigned lifetime value

fields.name: signup_date
fields.title: Signup Date
fields.description: Date when customer registered, YYYY-MM-DD (2020-01-01 to 2024-12-30)

fields.name: gender
fields.title: Gender
fields.description: Customer gender: F, M, Prefer not to say, or Non-binary (4 values)

fields.name: country
fields.title: Country
fields.description: Customer country code, 10 values: US, UK, CA, DE, FR, AU, JP, BR, IN, MX

fields.name: segment
fields.title: Customer Segment
fields.description: Customer value segment, 5 values: Regular, Budget Shopper, Premium, VIP, Occasional Visitor (churn rate varies by segment)

fields.name: lifetime_value
fields.title: Lifetime Value
fields.description: Assigned customer lifetime value in USD (71.21-9353.25). Generated from the customer's segment, not summed from transactions.csv - it correlates with realized completed spend at r=0.56, so treat it as a segment proxy rather than a derived total

fields.name: email_opt_in
fields.title: Email Opt-In
fields.description: Whether customer opted into email marketing (0/1)

fields.name: has_app
fields.title: Has App
fields.description: Whether customer has installed mobile app (0/1)

resources.description: 1,000 product catalog rows across 15 categories and 20 brands, with pricing, discounts, ratings and stock

fields.name: category
fields.title: Category
fields.description: Product category, 15 values: Electronics, Clothing, Home & Garden, Books, Sports, Beauty, Toys, Food & Grocery, Office Supplies, Automotive, Health, Pet Supplies, Jewelry, Music, Software

resources.description: 120,000 purchase transactions with amounts, discounts, payment methods and order status

fields.name: transaction_date
fields.title: Transaction Date
fields.description: Date and time of transaction, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (2023-01-01 to 2024-12-30)

fields.name: unit_price
fields.title: Unit Price
fields.description: Price per unit in USD. Exactly products.price x (1 - discount_applied/100) for every row - derivable from the join, so exclude it when predicting price

fields.name: status
fields.title: Status
fields.description: Transaction status: completed (57.2%), refunded (14.3%), cancelled (14.2%), pending (14.2%)

fields.name: payment_method
fields.title: Payment Method
fields.description: Payment method, 6 values: credit_card, debit_card, paypal, apple_pay, google_pay, bank_transfer

resources.description: 80,000 browsing sessions with device, channel, duration, pages and conversion flags

fields.name: session_date
fields.title: Session Date
fields.description: Date and time session started, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS (2023-01-01 to 2024-12-30)

fields.name: channel
fields.title: Traffic Channel
fields.description: Acquisition channel, 6 values: organic, paid_search, social, direct, email, referral

fields.name: pages_viewed
fields.title: Pages Viewed
fields.description: Number of pages viewed in session (1-142)

fields.name: cart_additions
fields.title: Cart Additions
fields.description: Number of items added to cart (0-5)

resources.description: 25,000 product reviews with 1-5 star ratings, template text and helpfulness votes

fields.name: review_date
fields.title: Review Date
fields.description: Date review was submitted, YYYY-MM-DD (2023-01-01 to 2024-12-30)

fields.name: review_text
fields.title: Review Text
fields.description: Customer review text, drawn from 15 rating-consistent template sentences - usable for sentiment pipelines but not for realistic NLP benchmarking

fields.name: helpful_votes
fields.title: Helpful Votes
fields.description: Number of helpful votes from other customers (0-49)

authors.name: Lorenzo Scaturchio
authors.bio: Independent ML engineer building synthetic, education-first datasets for reproducible benchmarking and prototyping.

sources: Synthetic data generation scripts in this repository
Public domain schemas and domain conventions for educational simulation
provenance.collection_methodology: Programmatic synthetic generation using seeded statistical distributions and rule-based constraints to mimic realistic structure while avoiding direct personal data.
